scene_context: En la oficina privada de Sandra Mills, gerente de Análisis Cuantitativo en una firma de consultoría de datos en Canary Wharf, Londres. Es el miércoles por la tarde, un día después del incidente, y acabas de cerrar la puerta.
expected_outcome_indicator: Secure informal mediation without escalating to formal HR complaint.
example_conversation:
Person: Come in, sit down. You look a bit preoccupied. Everything alright with the Westchester contract?
User: The project's fine, though something occurred yesterday in the team meeting that I felt needed your awareness before it festers. David made a comment about my accent—suggesting it slows communication—and whilst I don't believe he intended genuine malice, it's landed somewhat uncomfortably, particularly given the confidentiality of the client discussions we conduct.
Person: That's a serious accusation. Did anyone else hear this? I'll need to escalate it formally if we're talking about discriminatory behaviour.
User: I understand your obligation, though I'm hesitant to trigger the formal machinery unnecessarily. David and I work closely; I'd prefer to address this through a candid conversation where he understands the impact, rather than through a grievance procedure that might poison the team dynamic irreparably. Would a three-way discussion be possible where we reset expectations about professional language without litigating intent?
Person: I appreciate you wanting to handle this maturely, but you're putting me in a difficult position. If I don't document this and it continues, I'm liable.
User: That's a fair point, and I'm not asking you to ignore it. Perhaps we document that you've addressed it informally, and establish a clear boundary that a second incident triggers the formal pathway? That way you're protected procedurally, and David gets a genuine chance to correct course.
Person: Alright, I'll speak with him today. Let's see how he responds, and we'll reconvene on Friday.

title: Explicar el rechazo académico y solicitar otra oportunidad de publicación
description: Te han rechazado el artículo en Contemporary Linguistics Quarterly. Escribes al editor para refutar al revisor y pedir un segundo dictamen.
objective: Escribir un correo persuasivo al editor jefe de la revista *Contemporary Linguistics Quarterly* (Dr. Hassan Al-Rashid) cuestionando gentilmente el fallo del reviewer anónimo que rechazó tu artículo sobre sintaxis comparativa ("Null Subjects Across Romance Microvariation: A Diachronic Corpus Study"), argumentando que sus críticas (a) malinterpretan tu metodología estadística en la página 7, (b) ignoran tres estudios recientes de 2023 que apoyan tu tesis, y (c) proponen un análisis alternativo que ya descartaste en la sección 3.2 por razones que explicas de nuevo, y solicitando un segundo dictamen peer-review antes de una decisión definitiva.
scene_context: En tu despacho de investigador en el departamento de Lingüística de la Universidad de Edinburgh, después de recibir el correo de rechazo hace una hora. Tu doctorado depende de publicaciones en revistas de Tier 1.
expected_outcome_indicator: Secure agreement for second peer review and resubmission opportunity.
example_conversation:
Person: Dear Dr. Morrison, thank you for your response to the editorial decision. I've reviewed your concerns. The reviewer's critique seemed quite robust to me.
User: I appreciate your candour, Dr. Al-Rashid, though I wonder whether the reviewer's assertion on page three—that my log-linear regression inadequately controls for sociolinguistic variables—reflects a careful reading of my Appendix C, where I explicitly enumerate the stratification criteria and report Variance Inflation Factors beneath accepted thresholds. It's possible my exposition was opaque, though the statistical foundation itself is sound.
Person: These technical disputes are difficult to adjudicate without the reviewer present. They might have had access to considerations we're not seeing in the final report.
User: Undoubtedly, though I'm particularly concerned that the reviewer dismisses the Lunelli and Rossi 2023 corpus analysis and the Moretti 2023 diachronic study—both published in your own journal—which substantially corroborate my findings on subject licensing asymmetries. Ignoring contemporaneous work that supports one's argument is precisely what peer review should catch. Additionally, their proposed alternative analysis using mixed-effects modelling—whilst methodologically valid—was my initial approach, which I abandoned following the piloting phase outlined in section 3.2 due to convergence failures on the full dataset.
Person: I see your point about the recent literature. I'm not entirely convinced the reviewer overlooked those papers intentionally, but I take your frustration. What would resolve this for you?
User: A second independent review, ideally from someone conversant with corpus methodology, would either validate the concerns or confirm that the initial assessment was perhaps overly dismissive. I'm prepared to substantially revise the clarity of my statistical reporting, and I can integrate the recent literature more prominently. Rather than a final rejection, might a "revise and resubmit" with a second reader be feasible?
Person: That's fair. I'll solicit another opinion. Don't revise yet—wait for the second reader's input.

title: Impugnar una decisión de denegación de visa y solicitar revisión
description: El Reino Unido rechazó tu visa Skilled Worker patrocinada por tu empleador. Preparas una carta formal para pedir la revisión del expediente.
objective: Enviar una carta formal al oficial de visas (Centro de Visas Británicas en Madrid, oficina de Cristina Márquez) solicitando una revisión de tu denegación de visa Skilled Worker (categoría de la que tu empleador Deloitte Madrid confirmó que calificas), argumentando que la conclusión de que "tu experiencia no es relevante para el puesto de Senior Consultant" contradice tu CV que enumera 7 años en consultoría de transformación digital, tres certificaciones profesionales (PMP, Agile, Cloud Architecture), y cartas de recomendación de dos directivos de Fortune 500 incluidas en el dossier original.
scene_context: En tu apartamento en Madrid, después de recibir la notificación de denegación del Reino Unido hace tres días. Tu empleador está esperando tu aprobación antes de formalizar la mudanza y el inicio laboral el 1 de octubre.
expected_outcome_indicator: Request administrative review with documented evidence of qualifications.
example_conversation:
Person: This is the visa office line. May I help you?
User: Yes, I'm calling regarding my application reference VW-2024-456789, which was refused yesterday. I believe there's been a substantive error in the assessment, and I'd like to request a formal administrative review before proceeding with reapplication.
Person: I'm afraid refusals are rarely overturned. What's your concern with the decision?
User: The refusal states that my experience is insufficiently relevant to the role, yet my documentation—a seven-year consultancy background in digital transformation, three professional certifications, and endorsement letters from two C-suite executives—directly mirrors the Skilled Worker requirements outlined by my sponsor, Deloitte Madrid. The justification appears to have overlooked the supporting evidence or misinterpreted my CV.
Person: Did you provide a detailed role description from your employer?
User: Absolutely. The job specification is attached to my application demonstrating point-for-point alignment with my background. Moreover, my employer's assigned sponsor licence permits precisely this occupational category, and they've confirmed in writing that my profile exceeds their baseline criteria. While I respect the visa officer's gatekeeping role, I'd argue the refusal doesn't address the substantive qualifications documentation, which warrants at minimum a second review before I withdraw and reapply incurring further costs.
Person: Submit a written request for review within ten working days, attaching a supplementary statement addressing the specific refusal grounds. That's your recourse.
User: I intend to do exactly that. Should the review officer require clarification or additional evidence—testimonials, project portfolios, or academic transcripts—what's the preferred submission channel and expected turnaround time?

title: Negociar términos de una beca de investigación
description: Beca doctoral: 800 euros al mes, contrato de 36 meses y laboratorio a tope. Negocias con el Dr. Matthews las condiciones antes de firmar.
objective: Convencer al coordinador (Dr. Matthews) de que aumente tu asignación mensual de 800 a 1000 euros, añada 2 meses de prórroga al contrato de 36 meses, y asegure acceso garantizado a los equipos del laboratorio de microscopía antes de septiembre, justificando cada petición con argumentos académicos concretos.
scene_context: Estás en la oficina del Dr. Matthews, coordinador de investigación doctoral en una universidad británica, después de que te haya notificado cambios en la financiación disponible.
expected_outcome_indicator: Secure increased funding, contract extension, and lab access guarantees through reasoned negotiation.
example_conversation:
Person: I appreciate your time today. As you know, we're facing some budgetary constraints across the doctoral scheme this year, which means we may need to revisit certain allocations.
User: I understand the fiscal pressures, Dr. Matthews, but I'd like to present a case for why the additional 200 euros monthly wouldn't merely constitute a personal convenience—it's essential for conducting rigorous fieldwork in my methodology.
Person: I'm listening, though I should mention that any adjustment would need to be offset by demonstrable gains in productivity or publication trajectory.
User: Precisely my point. The supplementary funds would enable me to secure access to the tissue samples repository at the biotech facility, which, whilst technically available, requires a licensing fee that my current allocation simply doesn't accommodate—without it, my comparative analysis becomes untenable.
Person: That's a more compelling rationale than I'd anticipated. As for the contract extension, that's considerably trickier given the departmental mandate.
User: I recognise the constraints, yet if I might respectfully suggest: postponing the completion date by merely two months would align my thesis submission with the spring publication cycle, thereby maximising the department's research output when it comes to the annual review metrics—not to mention that it mitigates the risk of rushed conclusions.

title: Impugnar una evaluación de desempeño laboral
description: Tu evaluación anual te dejó en "satisfactorio" pese a subir ventas un 23%. Estás con Sarah Chen para impugnarla con evidencia y pedir una revisión.
objective: Debes impugnar la evaluación de desempeño recibida el 15 de marzo argumentando que tus logros (incremento de ventas del 23%, liderazgo de 3 proyectos exitosos y reducción de costos de $50,000) no se reflejan en la calificación "satisfactorio", y solicitar explícitamente una reclasificación a "excepcional" o una revisión por un tercero en las próximas dos semanas.
scene_context: Estás en la oficina de tu manager, Sarah Chen, después de recibir tu evaluación anual. La tensión es evidente pero profesional.
expected_outcome_indicator: Successfully challenge unfair appraisal with documented evidence and negotiate review timeline.
example_conversation:
Person: I've reviewed your annual evaluation, and while your contributions have been solid, we felt your initiative has been somewhat limited this cycle.
User: I appreciate your feedback, but I'm afraid I must respectfully contest that characterization. Not only did I spearhead the market expansion initiative that yielded a 23% revenue uptick, but I also mitigated significant procurement bottlenecks, which netted us $50,000 in cost savings—metrics that are, frankly, difficult to reconcile with a "satisfactory" rating.
Person: Well, those are certainly notable achievements, but we need to see more strategic thinking and cross-departmental collaboration.
User: With respect, I led three cross-functional projects this year, all of which concluded ahead of schedule and within budget. I'm concerned that the evaluation doesn't accurately reflect the quantifiable outcomes. I'd like to request an expedited review—either by yourself with additional documentation, or by an independent third party within the next two weeks—to ensure the assessment aligns with the evidence.
Person: That's a fair point. I'll discuss it with upper management and get back to you by Friday.
User: Thank you. I appreciate your willingness to reconsider, and I'm confident that once you examine the project reports and stakeholder feedback, the discrepancy will become evident.

title: Defender tu argumento sobre un cambio de estructura organizacional en tu empresa
description: La reestructuración centralizada ya ha costado tres bajas senior en dos meses. Defiendes ante la CEO un modelo alternativo con números.
objective: Debes argumentar que el nuevo modelo centralizado perjudicará la retención de talento (ya han renunciado 3 empleados senior en 2 meses), aumentará el tiempo de respuesta a clientes de 24 a 72 horas, y afectará la productividad del equipo de tu división en un 35% según tus proyecciones. Propone mantener 2 equipos descentralizados con supervisión coordinada, requiriendo un presupuesto adicional de 80.000€ anuales pero generando ahorros de 250.000€ evitando rotación de personal.
scene_context: Estás en una reunión de junta directiva con la CEO, Margaret Chen, quien ya implementó la reestructuración hace 3 semanas sin retroalimentación.
expected_outcome_indicator: Presented compelling ROI argument grounded in attrition data and operational metrics, challenging centralization strategy with feasible decentralized alternative.
example_conversation:
Person: The restructuring is already in motion, and I'm confident it will yield significant efficiencies. I'm not sure what prompted you to revisit this now, frankly.
User: I respect the decision, but the data from the first three weeks warrants a reconsideration; we've already lost three senior team members, and our customer response time has ballooned from 24 to 72 hours—figures that directly contradict the efficiency promise.
Person: These are early growing pains; people adapt, and we'll optimize response protocols as we go.
User: Granted that adjustment periods are inevitable, yet the attrition pattern is alarming when contextualized against industry benchmarks; replacing a mid-level analyst costs roughly 150 percent of their annual salary, so three departures alone have cost us 320.000€ in recruitment and onboarding—a figure that rather undercuts any savings the centralization was meant to achieve.
Person: You're conflating separate issues; attrition happens regardless of structure.
User: Perhaps in the abstract, but my proposal isn't to jettison the restructuring wholesale; rather, it's to maintain two decentralized hubs with coordinated oversight, which would require 80.000€ additional annually but would likely prevent future attrition and restore client responsiveness, thereby netting a 250.000€ saving relative to the costs of turnover we're currently incurring.

title: Cuestionar una política de crédito corporativo restrictiva
description: Los límites de crédito discrecional ahogan los proyectos innovadores de tu área. Negocias con el director financiero ampliarlos de $50.000 a $150.000.
objective: Convence al director financiero de ampliar los límites de crédito discrecional de $50.000 a $150.000 para tu departamento, argumenta que los criterios actuales frenan la innovación y propón un seguimiento trimestral para justificar cada ampliación.
scene_context: Estás en la oficina del director financiero de una empresa multinacional. Necesitas justificar por qué la política actual es contraproducente para la estrategia de innovación.
expected_outcome_indicator: Persuade Director to reconsider discretionary spending limits through reasoned argumentation.
example_conversation:
Person: I appreciate your proposal, but frankly, the current thresholds have been in place for precisely this reason—to mitigate frivolous expenditure. What makes you think loosening them would benefit rather than compromise our fiscal prudence?
User: I understand your concern about fiscal discipline, but I'd argue the criteria are so restrictive that we're inadvertently handicapping ourselves relative to competitors who move faster on emerging opportunities. The $50,000 ceiling, which hasn't been indexed since 2019, effectively prevents us from piloting technologies that could yield substantial ROI within eighteen months.
Person: Those are rather broad claims. Do you have empirical evidence that our caution is costing us market share, or are you largely speculating?
User: Not entirely—I've analyzed three quarters of rejected proposals that would've fallen into the $50,000 to $150,000 band, and eighteen percent of them addressed client pain points our competitors subsequently captured. Granted, not all would have succeeded, but the opportunity cost of blanket rejection far exceeds the downside risk of selective, monitored access to those funds.
Person: You make a fair point, though I'd need to see that analysis in detail before committing to anything. Let's say I'm willing to entertain a pilot phase—perhaps with stricter governance mechanisms and quarterly reviews rather than an outright increase.
User: That's a constructive approach, and I'm genuinely grateful. I'd propose we trial this with a $100,000 threshold for Q3 and Q4, coupled with a steering committee that vets proposals against predefined innovation criteria. If the metrics validate the hypothesis—adoption rates, cost savings, or new revenue streams—we revisit the permanent threshold thereafter.

title: Defender tu posición en un debate ético corporativo
description: En la sala de juntas, accionistas y consejeros presionan por márgenes. Defiendes invertir 2,5 millones en sostenibilidad reconociendo sus dudas.
objective: Debes explicar por qué tu empresa debería invertir 2,5 millones de euros en prácticas sostenibles durante los próximos 18 meses, a pesar de que reducirá márgenes de ganancia en un 8%, reconociendo simultáneamente las preocupaciones de los accionistas sobre dividendos trimestrales y competitividad de mercado.
scene_context: Estás en una sala de juntas con el director financiero y tres miembros del consejo asesor que cuestionan tus propuestas de sostenibilidad. Necesitas persuadir sin sonar ingenuo.
expected_outcome_indicator: Successfully balanced ethical imperative with business reality and secured cautious consideration.
example_conversation:
Person: Look, I appreciate the sentiment, but frankly, sinking €2.5 million into sustainability initiatives when our competitors are cutting costs seems tone-deaf to shareholder concerns. What's your contingency if this doesn't yield ROI within three years?
User: I understand the trepidation, and you're right to raise it. However, what I'm proposing isn't altruism divorced from strategy; it's a calculated hedge against regulatory liability and reputational risk, both of which, as you know, have increasingly tangible financial implications. The €2.5 million represents a discretionary allocation that, mitigated through phased procurement and operational efficiency gains, would effectively cost us 4.2% rather than the full 8%.
Person: Phased, you say? Walk me through the timeline and where you'd absorb the losses initially.
User: Precisely. Q1 and Q2 focus on supply-chain audits and vendor renegotiation—minimal outlay. By Q3, we transition to carbon-neutral logistics, which admittedly incurs upfront costs, but the long-term savings on energy procurement offset roughly 60% by month eighteen. As for the remaining 40%, that's where reputational capital and risk mitigation converge; institutional investors increasingly penalize opacity on ESG metrics.
Person: And if the market doesn't reward that posture?
User: Then we've still fortified ourselves against what's now virtually inevitable regulatory tightening, whilst our competitors scramble to retrofit. We're not betting on virtue signalling; we're inoculating the firm.

title: Escalación de queja grave a gestión superior
description: Llevas seis semanas reportando una máquina defectuosa en la línea 3 y tu supervisora no actúa. Escalas el caso al director general con evidencia.
objective: Debes documentar e informar al director general que durante 6 semanas has reportado malfuncionamiento crítico en la maquinaria de la línea 3, presentar evidencia de tres incidentes sin lesiones graves, e insistir en una auditoría independiente de seguridad antes del 15 de enero, sin acusar directamente a tu supervisora de negligencia deliberada.
scene_context: Estás en el despacho del director general en una fábrica de manufactura. Tu supervisora directa no está presente. El director general te conoce de vista pero no íntimamente.
expected_outcome_indicator: Escalation accepted, independent safety audit scheduled, documented complaint formally recorded.
example_conversation:
Person: Your supervisor mentioned you've raised some concerns about Line 3. I've reviewed her assessment and she seems confident the equipment is within tolerance. What specifically are we discussing here?
User: With respect, sir, I believe there's a discrepancy in how the data's been interpreted. I've documented three instances—November 8th, 12th, and December 3rd—where the hydraulic coupling has misfired, each time creating momentary pressure spikes that, fortunately, haven't yet resulted in serious injury. However, what troubles me is the trajectory: the incidents are increasing in frequency, and my supervisor, though conscientious, may be deferring to manufacturer specifications rather than observable degradation.
Person: You're suggesting she's been dismissive, then.
User: I'm suggesting, sir, that there may be an institutional blind spot—not malice, but perhaps an over-reliance on the equipment's certification history. I've requested a formal maintenance log review three times. What I'm asking is for an independent third-party safety audit before we resume full-capacity production. The liability exposure, frankly, is significant.
Person: Independent audit is expensive and signals doubt about our protocols.
User: Understandably. However, the cost of a single serious injury—both human and legal—would dwarf the audit expenditure many times over. I'm not asking to shut down; I'm asking for verification. If the equipment passes, everyone sleeps better. If it doesn't, we've averted a catastrophe. That's not hyperbole; it's prudent governance.

title: Entrevista senior: argumentar experiencia no convencional
description: Entrevista para director de operaciones con un currículum de rotaciones en lugar de ascensos lineales. Toca convertir esa ruta en tu ventaja.
objective: Debes explicar cómo tus 12 años en tres empresas diferentes, con cambios de rol cada 3-4 años, te han preparado mejor para este puesto de director de operaciones que un candidato con ascenso lineal, mencionando específicamente el aprendizaje adquirido en gestión de cambio organizacional, adaptabilidad cultural y pensamiento sistémico.
scene_context: Estás en una entrevista con la directora de RRHH y el CEO de una empresa de tecnología mediana. Ambos han hecho una pregunta directa sobre la falta de linealidad en tu currículum.
expected_outcome_indicator: Reframed career narrative as strategic asset; demonstrated meta-competence in organizational complexity.
example_conversation:
Person: I'll be candid—your CV shows three companies in twelve years, lateral moves rather than progression. Some hiring managers might interpret that as restlessness or inability to commit. How do you see it?
User: Fair question, and I appreciate the directness. What appears as lateral movement is actually deliberately curated exposure to different operational architectures. Each transition wasn't flight; it was strategic infiltration of a new ecosystem. At TechCore, I optimized supply-chain procurement; at Nordic, I restructured customer operations for a distributed model; at Ascent, I navigated a post-acquisition integration where two entirely different cultures had to coalesce.
Person: So you're framing instability as intentional learning. But how does that translate to staying put and delivering in this role?
User: Because what I've acquired isn't just technical acumen—it's immunity to institutional inertia. Most directors of operations inherit a system and tweak it. I've built systems from misaligned fragments. I understand not just *how* operations function, but *why* they resist change, and critically, which resistance is structural versus cultural. When you inherit a role in a growing firm, you won't need someone who optimizes yesterday's paradigm; you'll need someone who can diagnose why stakeholders disagree on what optimization even means.
Person: That's elegant, but it's still a bet on someone who hasn't held a position longer than four years.
User: True. But consider: I'm not asking you to bet on loyalty to a title; I'm asking you to leverage someone whose liability *is* their ability to operate across organizational fractures. In eighteen months, you'll have clarity on whether that's valuable or whether you need institutional continuity. Either way, you'll have de-risked the decision through my track record of successful integrations.

title: Negociar los términos de un contrato de suministro
description: Renovación del contrato de suministro y las condiciones se te escapan. Defiendes plazos más cortos, responsabilidad limitada y fuerza mayor.
objective: Negocia la renovación del contrato: reduce el plazo de entrega de 90 a 60 días, limita la responsabilidad máxima a €50.000, blinda una cláusula de fuerza mayor para ambas partes y confirma los nuevos términos por escrito.
scene_context: Estás en una sala de conferencias corporativa con el Procurement Director del principal proveedor de materias primas. Es la tercera ronda de negociaciones y necesitas cerrar el acuerdo esta semana.
expected_outcome_indicator: Successfully negotiated delivery timeline, liability cap, and force majeure clause.
example_conversation:
Person: I appreciate your concerns, but I must emphasize that our standard terms reflect industry norms and mitigate our exposure considerably. Frankly, reducing the delivery window to sixty days would necessitate restructuring our entire supply chain, which frankly isn't discretionary for us.
User: I understand the constraints, yet what you're characterizing as industry standard doesn't align with what we're seeing elsewhere. Moreover, if we're to commit to a three-year contract of this magnitude, we need the flexibility that a sixty-day window provides, particularly given the volatility in our sector.
Person: That's a fair point, though I'd argue that the liability cap of one hundred thousand is precisely calibrated to compensate for unforeseen disruptions without bankrupting us operationally.
User: That's where I must respectfully push back. A hundred thousand doesn't adequately reflect the scale of our potential losses, nor does it incentivize the quality assurance we're investing in. What if we compromise at fifty thousand, but only if we include a robust force majeure clause that protects both parties?
Person: You're not wrong that a force majeure provision would assuage certain concerns. I could potentially advocate internally for seventy-five days and fifty thousand if you're amenable to accepting the liability as written.
User: That's movement, and I appreciate it. Seventy-five days is workable, provided we lock in the fifty thousand cap and ensure the force majeure language explicitly covers supply chain disruptions, which frankly, is increasingly relevant given geopolitical uncertainties we've all witnessed.

title: Negociar cláusulas de un contrato de obra con un arquitecto
description: Recibes el borrador del contrato de reforma de tu casa (€85.000) y hay cláusulas ambiguas. Cuestionas las tres más peligrosas antes de firmar.
objective: Cuestiona al menos tres cláusulas del contrato (plazos de entrega, responsabilidad por daños y resolución de disputas), propón enmiendas concretas para cada una y deja claro que no firmas los €85.000 sin cambios.
scene_context: Estás en la oficina de un arquitecto renombrado tras recibir un borrador de contrato para la renovación de tu propiedad. Necesitas aclarar términos que consideras onerosos.
expected_outcome_indicator: Successfully challenge vague contract terms and propose three concrete amendments.
example_conversation:
Person: Well, I've drafted a fairly standard agreement for the full renovation, which as you know encompasses the structural assessment, interior redesign, and project management through to completion.
User: I appreciate the comprehensiveness, but I'm concerned about the liability clause—specifically section 4.3, which appears to place all responsibility for unforeseen structural damage exclusively on my shoulders, despite my having engaged your firm precisely to mitigate such risks. Could we redefine that?
Person: That clause is fairly boilerplate in the industry, though I understand your apprehension. What sort of amendment were you envisioning?
User: I'd propose a tiered liability model whereby structural issues attributable to poor initial assessment fall under your purview, whereas those stemming from pre-existing conditions I failed to disclose remain mine. Additionally, the delivery timeline is vague—would you be amenable to inserting penalty clauses for overruns beyond three months?
Person: Penalty clauses do add complexity, but they're not unreasonable given the €85,000 investment involved. However, I'd need to insert a force majeure clause to protect us both from unforeseen circumstances.
User: Absolutely, provided we define force majeure narrowly to exclude supply chain delays, which are rather predictable in this market. That brings me to my third concern: the dispute resolution mechanism. Rather than litigation, might we include mandatory mediation before proceeding to arbitration?

title: Pedir un café para llevar
description: Vas con prisa por la mañana y quieres un café para llevar. Pide un café grande con leche, escucha el precio, paga y pregunta a qué hora cierran.
objective: Pide al camarero un café grande con leche para llevar, escucha el precio y paga, y pregunta también a qué hora cierran hoy.
scene_context: Entras con prisa a la cafetería antes del trabajo. Hay dos personas delante y el camarero sonríe.
example_conversation:
Barista: Good morning! What can I get you?
User: A coffee, please. To go.
Barista: Small or large?
User: Large, please. With milk.
Barista: That's three dollars.
User: Here you go. Thank you!

title: Comprar fruta en el mercado
description: Es sábado por la mañana y toca comprar fruta en el mercado. Compra manzanas y plátanos, compara precios con las naranjas y ajústate a 5 dólares.
objective: Compra un kilo de manzanas y medio de plátanos, pregunta el precio de cada uno, pide una bolsa si hace falta, compara con las naranjas y decide sin pasarte de 5 dólares.
scene_context: Sábado en el mercado de barrio, con puestos llenos y mucho ruido. El de la fruta te saluda.
example_conversation:
Fruit Vendor: Hello! The apples are very fresh today.
User: How much are they?
Fruit Vendor: Two dollars a kilo.
User: I want one kilo, please.
Fruit Vendor: Anything else?
User: No, thank you. That's all.

title: Registrarte en un hotel
description: Llegas al hotel de noche y quieres instalarte rápido. Da tu nombre, confirma las dos noches y resuelve desayuno, wifi y servicio de habitaciones.
objective: Da tu nombre y confirma la reserva de dos noches, pregunta a qué hora es el desayuno, pide la contraseña del wifi y pregunta si hay servicio de habitaciones.
scene_context: Llegas al hotel con la maleta después de seis horas de tren. La recepción está tranquila.
example_conversation:
Receptionist: Good evening! Do you have a reservation?
User: Yes, my name is Laura.
Receptionist: Room 305. Here is your key.
User: What time is breakfast?
Receptionist: From seven to ten.
User: Perfect, thank you.

title: Pedir comida en un restaurante
description: Comes en un restaurante donde no conoces los platos. Pide pollo con ensalada, esquiva lo picante cambiando a arroz y remata con el postre del día.
objective: Pide pollo con ensalada y agua, pregunta si el pollo lleva salsa, cambia a arroz si lleva picante, pregunta el postre del día y pide pan.
scene_context: Restaurante de barrio a mediodía con manteles a cuadros. El camarero se acerca con la libreta.
example_conversation:
Waiter: Good afternoon! Are you ready to order?
User: Yes. I want the chicken, please.
Waiter: With rice or salad?
User: With salad, please.
Waiter: And to drink?
User: Water, please. No dessert.

title: Comprar una camiseta
description: Quieres una camiseta azul y la primera talla no te convence. Pregunta el precio, pruébate otra talla, averigua si hay descuento y decide con calma.
objective: Pide una camiseta azul talla mediana, pregunta el precio, si no te queda pide otra en el probador, pregunta si hay descuento y decide si la compras.
scene_context: Tienda de ropa con música suave; un montón de camisetas dobladas y dos probadores al fondo.
example_conversation:
Shop Assistant: Hi! Can I help you?
User: Yes, I like this blue T-shirt.
Shop Assistant: What size are you?
User: Medium, please.
Shop Assistant: Here you go. The fitting room is there.
User: Thank you!

title: Preguntar por la parada del bus
description: Te mudas de barrio y necesitas dominar el autobús. Pregunta dónde está la parada, cada cuánto pasa, cuánto cuesta y si el billete vale para dos viajes.
objective: Pregunta dónde está la parada del bus, a qué hora pasa el próximo, cuánto cuesta el billete, si sirve el mismo para dos viajes y cuánto tiempo vale.
scene_context: Esquina del centro con coches y bicis. Una señora espera junto al semáforo con bolsas.
example_conversation:
Local: Excuse me, where is the bus stop?
User: It's next to the bank.
Local: Is it far?
User: No, two minutes walking.
Local: Thank you very much!
User: You're welcome.

title: En el médico: dolor de cabeza
description: Llevas con dolor de cabeza desde anoche y vas al médico. Explica los síntomas, pregunta la dosis, si puedes conducir y cuándo volver si no mejora.
objective: Explica que te duele la cabeza desde anoche y si tomaste algo, pregunta cada cuánto tomar la medicina, si puedes conducir y cuándo volver si no mejora.
scene_context: Consulta del médico con estanterías y un reloj de pared. El doctor revisa tu historial.
example_conversation:
Doctor: Good morning. How do you feel?
User: I have a headache.
Doctor: When did it start?
User: Last night.
Doctor: Take this medicine twice a day.
User: Thank you, doctor.

title: Llamar a un amigo para quedar
description: Quieres organizar el sábado con tu amigo por teléfono. Propón el cine, acordad la hora y la película, y resolved quién compra las entradas.
objective: Llama a tu amigo, propón ir al cine el sábado, acordad la hora, pregunta qué película quiere ver, organiza dónde comprar las entradas y quién paga.
scene_context: Tarde en casa con el móvil en la mano: quieres cerrar el plan del sábado.
example_conversation:
Friend: Hello? It's me, Sam.
User: Hi Sam! How are you?
Friend: Good! Do you want to go to the cinema?
User: Yes! What time?
Friend: At eight, on Saturday.
User: Perfect, see you there.

title: Comprar un billete de tren
description: Sales hoy hacia Brighton y no quieres perder tiempo. Compra ida y vuelta, pregunta por el descuento, el próximo tren, el andén y los cambios de vía.
objective: Compra un billete de ida y vuelta a Brighton para hoy, pregunta si hay descuento, la hora del próximo tren, el andén y si hay que cambiar de vía.
scene_context: Estación grande con paneles de salidas y gente corriendo. La taquillera te mira esperando.
example_conversation:
Ticket Clerk: Hello! Where do you want to go?
User: One ticket to Brighton, please.
Ticket Clerk: Single or return?

Ticket Clerk: That's twenty pounds. Platform 4.
User: Thank you!

title: Tu primer día de clase
description: Es tu primer día en una escuela de inglés. Preséntate a tu compañera, hablad del profesor y la clase y pregunta por las pausas y los baños.
objective: Preséntate a la compañera, pregúntale su nombre y de dónde es, hablad de la clase y del profesor, pregunta el horario de las pausas y dónde están los baños.
scene_context: Aula luminosa con mesas pequeñas y un mapa de Inglaterra. Faltan cinco minutos para empezar.
example_conversation:

title: Facturar una maleta en el aeropuerto
description: Estás en el mostrador del aeropuerto facturando tu equipaje. Entrega el pasaporte, factura la maleta y aclara el peso, la puerta y el embarque.
objective: Entrega el pasaporte, factura una maleta, pregunta si pesa demasiado, si va incluida en el billete, cuál es la puerta y a qué hora embarcas.
scene_context: Aeropuerto amplio con pantallas y cola en el mostrador. El equipaje de mano ya va contigo.

User: Here it is.
Check-in Agent: How many bags?

Check-in Agent: Your gate is B12. Have a good flight!

title: Pagar la cuenta del restaurante
description: La comida estaba buena y toca pagar. Dile al camarero que estaba deliciosa, pide la cuenta, paga con tarjeta y pide una copia del recibo.
objective: Dile al camarero que la comida estaba deliciosa, pide la cuenta, paga con tarjeta y pide una copia del recibo para guardarlo.
scene_context: Cena a media luz con vistas a la calle. Ya no queréis postre, solo ir a casa.

title: Alquilar una bicicleta
